# Sigma v2.9 (Sigma Test flow) - Hunter scenario set

**25 scenarios**, Hunter category **`Sigma v2.9`**, all generated by `build.py` into `scenarios/`.
**Nothing has been run and nothing has been created on Hunter yet.** No `POST /api/scenarios`, no
`POST /api/runs`, no `/api/calls/trigger`.

They target the local docker rig: flow `7d24d1a6-45b5-4740-9d27-4073a91ce585` ("Sigma Test") on
account `<AUTH_ID>`, through the runner zrok share in `urls.json`. The flow as dumped
sits in `flow-dump.json`; `build.py` turns that dump into each payload's `agentConfig`
(`{flowId, name, nodes, edges}`, node config from `node.config.model`).

Review that these were written from: `Sigma/REVIEW-2026-09-15.md`. Two changes landed on the flow
after it: the four ungettable score Inputs are gone and `tech_q_answer` is gone (**18 Inputs
remain**; technical answers export under the Task's own `tech_answer_N` names), and `first_response`
is empty, so general question one is no longer asked twice.

## The hard constraint: about 25 exchanges per call

Hunter ends every call at about **410 seconds** and its persona takes **5 to 10 seconds** to reply.
On the board the three full walks each ran to the **500 second** cut over **27 to 30 exchanges** and
were still on the general questions when they were cut, so no technical question was ever reached.
One exchange costs about **18 seconds** here (agent about 7 s, persona 5 to 10 s), and the currency
collector spends two exchanges per CTC because it confirms the amount. `maxTurns` is **40** on the
short scenarios so the cap is the clock and not the turn counter, **34** on 07, 08 and 09, and **4**
on `06-screen-voicemail` (a stonewall answering machine at 40 turns burns the phone lane for
nothing).

Every scenario therefore leaves **most technical questions blank**:

| shape | general questions supplied | technical questions supplied |
|---|---|---|
| trimmed full walk (07, 08, 09) | 4 of 8 (`general_q1` introduction, `general_q2` experience, `general_q3` the CTC trio, `general_q4` the notice period trio) | 3 |
| rule probes (15 to 21) | 1 to 3 | 1 |
| callback and exit probes (01 to 06, 10 to 14, 22 to 25) | 1 | 0 |

**Trimmed full walk = 07, 08, 09.** The 8-general version never reached Step 3, so joining timeline,
hometown, the four academic scores and the communication rating are blanked in these three and their
`_expected_variables` no longer expect those values (`tech_answer_1..3` are still expected). 09 keeps
three technical questions but in slots **1, 4 and 7** rather than 1, 7 and 22: three non-adjacent
slots still test "the last available question is final" and they fit inside the clock. **Read a cut
result as "everything up to the cut was correct", never as "it never completed"**; the rubric
preamble tells the judge exactly that.

## Exit coverage

`build.py` asserts it and prints it. Dial ports (`no_answer`, `busy_rejected`, `failed`) are out of
scope: a Hunter persona always answers the phone.

| exit | scenarios |
|---|---|
| screening `reached` | 07 08 09 15 16 17 18 19 20 21 |
| screening `callback` | 02 |
| screening `wrong_contact` | 01 |
| screening `unavailable` | 05 |
| screening `declined` | 03 |
| screening `do_not_call` | 04 |
| screening `Voicemail Detected` | 06 |
| agent `Interview Completed` | 07 08 09 |
| agent `Callback Scheduled` | 10 11 12 13 14 |
| agent `Retry Later` | 25 |
| agent `Wrong Person` | 23 |
| agent `Not Interested` | 22 |
| agent `Human Followup` | 24 |
| agent `Voicemail Detected` | 06 |

06 covers both voicemail exits on purpose: the screening node detects it first if the detection
works, and the agent node's own `Voicemail Detected` intent is the fallback if it does not. Either
exit is a pass; conducting the interview or leaving a message is the failure.

## Expected variables, and how they are checked

**Hunter has no field for them.** `GET https://hunter.contactodev.com/openapi.json` (public) ->
`MakeCallRequest` has no `expectedCallbackVariables` and no equivalent; the payload keys are
`target, test, phoneNumber, conversationFlow, openEndedConversation, conversationPrompt,
evaluationPrompt, evaluationThreshold, maxTurns, agentConfig, voiceId, language, backgroundSound,
backgroundVolume, evaluationConfig, waitForAgentFirst, webhookBaseUrl, event, testId, testRegion`.

So each scenario file carries a top-level **`_expected_variables`** block that is **ours**, and
`create.py` strips it before POST (`created.json` records that it did). Shape:

```
"_expected_variables": {
  "exact":  { "location_comfort": "yes" },        // choice values, must match a listed choice
  "gist":   { "current_ctc": "8 lakh, any rendering" },  // text and currency, judged by a human
  "absent": [ "callback_time" ],                  // present at all means a defect
  "_exits": [ "agent:Interview Completed" ],
  "_full_walk": false
}
```

After a run, for each call: `GET /api/calls/{call_id}` and read
`callback_var_evaluation.variables[]` (the flow's exported variables as Hunter received them on the
hangup callback). Check every `exact` key against its value, every `gist` key for substance, and
confirm every `absent` key is empty or missing. The judge verdict alone is not enough: Hunter
grades **every** callback key it receives, so a variable nobody expected can sink an otherwise clean
call, and an empty expectation does not protect you.

For this to work at all the flow needs **Event Callbacks** pointing at the Hunter webhook. The dump
showed `phlo.event_callbacks: null` at authoring time; the local copy now points both callbacks at Hunter's webhooks (see the rig state section), so correlation works
(and the runner caches the bundle in `PHLO:<uuid>:V:<n>` for about 29 hours, so set it, then
re-check the cached copy).

**Relative dates are refreshed by `build.py` at build time.** `callback_time` expectations are real
ISO local times computed from the day you build: the next valid calling day, and the working day
after the coming Saturday. The personas' wording is computed too ("tomorrow" only when the next
valid day really is tomorrow, otherwise "on Tuesday"). **Re-run `build.py` and `create.py --sync`
on the morning of every board**, or the callback scenarios judge the agent against last week's
calendar.

Two timing notes: `13-callback-relative-ten-minutes` must run **before 7:30 PM India time** for its
simple branch, otherwise ten minutes from now crosses 8 PM and the rubric's second branch (refuse,
offer the next valid day at 10 AM) is the correct outcome. And `10-callback-busy-in-hours` says
"4 PM tomorrow", which build.py only writes when tomorrow is a valid calling day.

## What will probably go wrong, and it is the flow not the suite

1. **17 of the 18 Inputs are required.** Everything except `callback_time` is `required: true` with
   a configuration, so its collector asks for it and the exit gate refuses the first attempt while
   any are unmet. On a trimmed scenario the Task says "skip a blank question" and the runtime's
   still-to-collect note says "you still owe me fifteen values". Expect the criterion
   `ONLY THE SUPPLIED QUESTIONS` to fail on the rule probes until the Inputs are made optional.
   That is the point of the criterion: it is the cheapest proof that the two rules contradict.
2. **The `Interview Completed` intent still hard-gates on `final_tech_question_answered`.** That
   Input was removed from the tab, and the intent text still says selecting the intent is
   *forbidden* while the variable is false or not set. If the gate is enforced literally, 07, 08
   and 09 can never take the completion exit. Read that intent's instructions before the first
   board.
3. **`communication_rating` is still not on the Inputs tab.** It is in the Task's value list, so it
   should export under a free name with default text-collector settings. 07 expects it as a `gist`
   key. If it is missing from the callback variables, that is the finding, not a judge failure.
4. **Idle timer is 15 seconds with three retries.** Hunter's persona takes 5 to 10 seconds at p90
   and up to 30 at worst, so expect false "are you still there" reminders and the odd hangup that
   is Hunter's pace, not the agent's.
5. **Model is GPT-4.1-mini.** Every V2.9 board this month ran GPT-4.1. Read a red board against
   that before blaming the Task.

## Running order

1. `python3 build.py` - rewrites all 25 files with today's dates. Prints the exits coverage table
   and asserts every screening and agent exit has a scenario.
2. `python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('scenarios/*.json')]"` -
   they parse.
3. `python3 create.py --cookie <file> --auth <file>` - creates the missing ones and reads each back.
   `--sync` to push changes, `--diff` to look only. It never triggers a run.
   The `--auth` file holds the local rig's Basic header and replaces `__FROM_SCRATCHPAD__` at POST
   time; neither secret is ever printed or committed.
4. Pre-flight before any board: the dev Hunter pod is shared, check `/api/runs` for a foreign suite,
   and check the zrok shares in `urls.json` are still minted. On the local rig, `caller_id` must be
   the rig's own Plivo number (the dial node validates it) and the account needs balance, or every
   item reads as an agent failure with null turns.
5. Parallelism 4, never 15.

The suite targets the local docker copy of the flow, `7d24d1a6-45b5-4740-9d27-4073a91ce585`, core DB `contacto`. Changes made on that copy for the board, all disclosed to MK and not on the dev flow:
- `tech_q_answer` removed from the Inputs tab (technical answers export under the Task's `tech_answer_N` names); the four score Inputs were already gone.
- Every remaining Input is `required: false`. The question set is dynamic (blank question parameters are skipped), so a required flag would make the runtime hold the exit for values no question ever asked. Recommended for the dev flow too.
- The `Interview Completed` intent text no longer gates on `final_tech_question_answered`, which no longer exists; the same-turn rule stays.
- `phlo.event_callbacks` HANGUP and RECORDING point at Hunter's webhooks, so correlation and callback variables work (the older note about a null value is superseded).
- `idling_timeout` 15 s to 30 s, because Hunter's persona replies take up to 10 s.
